questions.question: What is the primary function of the WTO?

options.text: To liberalise international trade and ensure fair practices

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To liberalise international trade and ensure fair practices**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The World Trade Organization (WTO) is an international body that governs global trade rules and agreements between member countries.
 
• Its primary objective is to liberalise international trade by reducing trade barriers such as tariffs, quotas, and subsidies, while ensuring fair competition.
 
• The WTO provides a platform for trade negotiations, dispute resolution, and transparency in trade policies to ensure smooth and predictable trade flows.
 
• It addresses unfair trade practices, including dumping and subsidies, which distort market competition, promoting a level playing field for all member nations.
 
• The WTO also assists developing countries with technical training and capacity-building programs to help them integrate into the global trading system effectively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Formation and Membership:**

 
 
• The WTO was established on January 1, 1995, replacing the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT).
 
• It currently has 164 member countries, accounting for over 98% of global trade as of 2023.
 
 
 
• **Core Principles:**
 
 
• The WTO operates on principles such as non-discrimination, free trade, and transparency to foster predictable and fair trade practices globally.
 
• It promotes the Most Favoured Nation (MFN) principle, ensuring equal treatment of all trading partners.

questions.question: Which festival of Nagaland usually begins on 1 December, every year?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hornbill Festival**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Hornbill Festival** is an annual cultural festival celebrated in Nagaland, India, starting on **1st December every year**.
 
• It is organized by the **Government of Nagaland** to preserve and promote the rich heritage and traditions of the **indigenous Naga tribes**.
 
• The festival is named after the **Great Hornbill bird**, which holds symbolic importance in Naga folklore and is admired for its beauty.
 
• The primary venue for the festival is the **Kisama Heritage Village**, located near Kohima, the capital of Nagaland.
 
• The Hornbill Festival includes various activities such as **traditional dances, music performances, craft exhibitions, sporting events, and local cuisine stalls**, attracting tourists from India and abroad.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bihu Festival:**

 
 
• Bihu is the most celebrated festival of Assam and signifies **agricultural prosperity**.
 
• There are three types of Bihu celebrated in Assam: **Bohag Bihu** (spring), **Magh Bihu** (harvest), and **Kati Bihu** (sowing).
 
• The Bohag Bihu marks the Assamese New Year and is celebrated with cultural performances, traditional dances, songs, and feasts.
 
• It is not related to Nagaland or the Hornbill Festival.
 
 
 
• **Losoong Festival:**
 
 
• Losoong is the **harvest festival of Sikkim**, celebrated by the Bhutia and Lepcha communities.
 
• It marks the end of the harvest season and the beginning of a new year in the traditional lunar calendar.
 
• Losoong is observed with rituals, dances, and sporting activities, including archery contests.
 
• It is not celebrated in Nagaland and is unrelated to the Hornbill Festival.
 
 
 
• **Wangala Festival:**
 
 
• Wangala is a harvest festival celebrated by the **Garo tribes** in Meghalaya.
 
• It is dedicated to the Sun God **Saljong** and marks the end of the agricultural season.
 
• The festival involves traditional dances, music, and rituals performed by the Garo community.
 
• Wangala is specific to Meghalaya and has no connection to the Hornbill Festival celebrated in Nagaland.
 
 
 
• **Kisama Heritage Village:**
 
 
• This cultural hub represents the traditions and lifestyles of all the **16 officially recognized Naga tribes**.
 
• During the Hornbill Festival, the village hosts exhibitions of tribal artifacts, traditional huts, handlooms, and local cuisines.
 
• It serves as a global platform to showcase the diverse cultural heritage of Nagaland.

questions.question: The Government of India Act, 1935 provided for how many lists of divisions of power between the federation (central government) and provinces?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Three lists**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Government of India Act, 1935 introduced a federal structure that divided powers between the center (federal government) and the provinces (states).
 
• This Act provided for **three lists** for the division of legislative subjects: the Federal List, the Provincial List, and the Concurrent List.
 
• The **Federal List** included 59 subjects such as defense, foreign affairs, and currency, on which only the central government could legislate.
 
• The **Provincial List** contained 54 subjects like police, education, and agriculture, where the provincial governments had exclusive powers.
 
• The **Concurrent List** had 36 subjects like criminal law, marriage, and bankruptcy, where both the central and provincial governments could legislate. In case of conflict, the federal law prevailed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Two lists**

 
 
• Before the Government of India Act, 1935, the **Government of India Act, 1919** introduced a dyarchy system, which divided subjects into two lists: *Reserved* and *Transferred*.
 
• The **Reserved List** included subjects like defense, foreign affairs, and revenue, which were under the control of the Governor-General.
 
• The **Transferred List** included subjects such as education, health, and local government, which were managed by Indian ministers under the control of provincial legislatures.
 
 
 
• **Government of India Act, 1935**
 
 
• The Government of India Act, 1935, was the longest and most detailed constitutional act passed by the British Parliament for Indian governance.
 
• It laid the foundation for federalism in India and introduced provincial autonomy, allowing provinces to self-govern in their legislative domains.
 
• While the act was revolutionary for its time, it faced criticism for retaining significant control with the British Crown, particularly in areas like defense and foreign affairs.

questions.question: Which of the following was the theme of the Ninth Five-year Plan?

options.text: Development of the public sector and rapid Industrialisation
Growth with social justice and equality
Promote inclusive growth and equitable development
Removal of poverty and attainment of self-reliance

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Growth with social justice and equality**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Ninth Five-Year Plan (1997-2002) was designed to achieve **“Growth with social justice and equality.”**
 
• It emphasized **poverty alleviation, employment generation, and human development** while maintaining a sustainable economic growth rate.
 
• The plan targeted a GDP growth rate of **6.5% per annum** and aimed to reduce regional disparities.
 
• Special focus was given to rural development, agriculture, healthcare, education, and empowering women through various initiatives.
 
• The plan emphasized improving the **quality of life** and equitable access to basic services for all citizens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Development of the public sector and rapid industrialization (Option 1):**

 
 
• This was the primary focus of the **Second Five-Year Plan (1956–1961)**, based on the Mahalanobis model.
 
• It aimed to promote **industrial growth** and emphasized the development of heavy industries and the public sector.
 
• The plan also focused on building infrastructure and capital goods industries to lay the foundation for long-term development.
 
 
 
• **Promote inclusive growth and equitable development (Option 3):**
 
 
• This was the theme of the **Eleventh Five-Year Plan (2007–2012)**.
 
• It focused on achieving faster and more inclusive growth by addressing inequalities in income, education, and healthcare.
 
• The plan emphasized **reducing poverty, empowering marginalized sections, and improving infrastructure development.**
 
 
 
• **Removal of poverty and attainment of self-reliance (Option 4):**
 
 
• This was the focus of the **Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974–1979).**
 
• The plan introduced the **Garibi Hatao (Remove Poverty)** slogan, aiming to reduce poverty and achieve self-reliance in food production.
 
• It emphasized national self-reliance, employment generation, and improving the living standards of the poor.

questions.question: Boiling and evaporation, respectively, are _______ and ______ phenomena.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**bulk and surface**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Boiling** is a bulk phenomenon, where the entire liquid participates in the process of vaporization, forming bubbles within the liquid, which rise and burst at the surface.
 
• **Evaporation** is a surface phenomenon as it involves only the molecules at the liquid's surface gaining sufficient energy to escape into the gaseous state.
 
• Boiling occurs at a specific temperature called the **boiling point**, whereas evaporation can happen at any temperature, depending on conditions like humidity and temperature.
 
• During boiling, external heat energy (latent heat of vaporization) is supplied uniformly to the liquid, while evaporation utilizes surrounding energy, often leading to a cooling effect.
 
• Boiling is fast and uniform across the liquid, whereas evaporation is slow and restricted to the surface.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Boiling:**

 
 
• Boiling occurs when the vapor pressure of the liquid equals the external atmospheric pressure.
 
• Bubbles of vapor form inside the liquid and rise to the surface, bursting to release the vapor.
 
• The boiling point is influenced by external pressure; lower atmospheric pressure decreases the boiling point (e.g., at high altitudes).
 
• Boiling is used in processes like distillation, sterilization, and cooking.
 
 
 
• **Evaporation:**
 
 
• Evaporation occurs when molecules at the liquid's surface gain enough kinetic energy to overcome intermolecular forces and escape into the gaseous phase.
 
• It leads to a cooling effect as the higher-energy molecules leave the liquid, reducing the average kinetic energy of the remaining molecules.
 
• The rate of evaporation increases with higher temperatures, larger surface area, and lower humidity.
 
• Evaporation plays a key role in processes like water cycle, cooling mechanisms, and drying of clothes.
 
 
 
• **Latent Heat of Vaporization:**
 
 
• This is the energy required to change a liquid into a vapor without altering its temperature.
 
• Latent heat of vaporization is essential in boiling, where external heat is supplied, and evaporation, where energy is absorbed from surroundings.
 
• It varies for different liquids and is higher for water compared to many other substances.

questions.question: Raga 'Laswanti' was composed by whom among the following personalities?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ustad Ali Akbar Khan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Raga 'Laswanti'** was composed by the legendary sarod maestro Ustad Ali Akbar Khan.
 
• Ustad Ali Akbar Khan was renowned for his mastery in Hindustani classical music and his ability to create innovative ragas.
 
• He was one of the first Indian musicians to bring Indian classical music to Western audiences, earning him global recognition.
 
• Known as the "Sarod Samrat" (Emperor of Sarod), his contributions to the Maihar Gharana and Indian music remain unparalleled.
 
• Raga 'Laswanti' is a unique creation that reflects his deep understanding of melody, rhythm, and the intricacies of Indian classical music.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ronu Majumdar:**

 
 
• Ronu Majumdar is a renowned Indian flautist specializing in the bansuri (bamboo flute).
 
• He belongs to the Maihar Gharana and has worked extensively in both Hindustani classical and fusion music.
 
• Although he is a master of classical ragas, he is not associated with the creation of Raga 'Laswanti'.
 
 
 
• **Tansen:**
 
 
• Tansen was one of the Navratnas (nine gems) in the court of Mughal Emperor Akbar and is considered one of the greatest composers in Indian classical music.
 
• He is credited with creating several ragas, including Miyan ki Todi and Darbari Kanada.
 
• However, Raga 'Laswanti' is not among the ragas attributed to Tansen.
 
 
 
• **Amjad Ali Khan:**
 
 
• Amjad Ali Khan is a celebrated sarod maestro known for his innovations in Indian classical music.
 
• He belongs to the Senia Bangash Gharana and is highly respected for his contributions to sarod playing.
 
• While he has performed and popularized many ragas, he is not associated with the creation of Raga 'Laswanti'.
 
 
 
• **Maihar Gharana:**
 
 
• Founded by Baba Allauddin Khan, the Maihar Gharana is a prominent school of Hindustani classical music.
 
• It emphasizes both vocal and instrumental music, with notable musicians such as Ustad Ali Akbar Khan, Pandit Ravi Shankar, and Annapurna Devi being associated with this gharana.
 
• The gharana is known for its innovative approach to traditional Indian music, as exemplified by creations like Raga 'Laswanti'.

questions.question: According to the census of India 2011, which north-east state of India among the following has the highest literacy rate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mizoram**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the Census of India 2011, Mizoram recorded the highest literacy rate among the north-eastern states, standing at **91.33%**.
 
• Mizoram ranks second in literacy rate across India, following Kerala, which holds the highest literacy rate at 94%.
 
• The state's exceptional literacy rate is a result of the collaborative efforts of the government, local communities, and the church in promoting education and literacy.
 
• Factors contributing to Mizoram's literacy achievements include free and compulsory education policies, universal enrollment initiatives, and the availability of schools even in remote areas.
 
• The Mizoram Education System places strong emphasis on retention, gender equality, and quality education, further boosting literacy levels in the state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Assam**

 
 
• Assam's literacy rate as per the Census of India 2011 is **72.19%**, which is below the national average of 74.04%.
 
• The state has made significant strides in education infrastructure but faces challenges such as poor access to remote areas and gender inequality in education.
 
• Government initiatives like 'Gunotsav' have been implemented to improve school performance and literacy levels.
 
 
 
• **Manipur**
 
 
• Manipur has a literacy rate of **79.85%**, according to the 2011 Census.
 
• Despite its relatively high literacy rate, challenges such as lack of infrastructure and political unrest have hindered further improvements.
 
• The state has focused on promoting education through schemes like the Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan (RMSA).
 
 
 
• **Nagaland**
 
 
• Nagaland recorded a literacy rate of **80.11%** in the 2011 Census.
 
• The state has shown commendable progress in literacy through initiatives aimed at promoting education in tribal and rural areas.
 
• However, challenges such as inadequate teacher training and low enrollment rates in higher education persist.
 
 
 
• **Literacy Rate in India (2011 Census)**
 
 
• The national literacy rate stands at **74.04%**, with Kerala leading at 94% and Bihar having the lowest literacy rate at 61.8%.
 
• North-eastern states have shown remarkable progress in education, with Mizoram, Tripura, and Nagaland surpassing the national average.
 
• Government initiatives like the Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan and the Right to Education Act have played a critical role in improving literacy rates across the country.

questions.question: YS Jagan Mohan Reddy, who lost his Chief Minister position in 2024, belongs to which of the following parties as of September 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Yuvajana Sramika Rythu Congress Party (YSRCP)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• YS Jagan Mohan Reddy is the leader of the **Yuvajana Sramika Rythu Congress Party (YSRCP)**, a regional political party based in Andhra Pradesh.
 
• The YSRCP was founded in 2011 by Jagan Mohan Reddy after he parted ways with the **Indian National Congress (INC)**.
 
• Under Jagan Mohan Reddy’s leadership, YSRCP won a historic victory in the 2019 Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly elections by securing **151 of the 175 assembly seats**.
 
• The party is known for its focus on welfare schemes and public service initiatives, such as **Amma Vodi** (financial assistance for education), **Rythu Bharosa** (support for farmers), and **Nadu-Nedu** (revamping school and hospital infrastructure).
 
• As of September 2024, Jagan Mohan Reddy continues to represent YSRCP, despite losing the Chief Minister position, and remains a significant political figure in Andhra Pradesh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jana Sena Party (JSP)**

 
 
• The Jana Sena Party was founded in 2014 by actor-turned-politician **Pawan Kalyan**.
 
• It is a regional political party in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana that focuses on anti-corruption measures, transparency, and the empowerment of youth.
 
• Despite its influence, JSP has not been able to secure a significant electoral victory in Andhra Pradesh till 2024.
 
 
 
• **Indian National Congress (INC)**
 
 
• INC is one of India’s oldest political parties, founded in 1885, and played a key role in the country’s independence movement.
 
• It has a significant presence across India but has largely lost its dominance in Andhra Pradesh after the bifurcation of the state in 2014.
 
• Jagan Mohan Reddy left INC in 2011 to form YSRCP following disagreements over leadership issues.
 
 
 
• **Telugu Desam Party (TDP)**
 
 
• TDP was founded in 1982 by N.T. Rama Rao and is one of the major political parties in Andhra Pradesh.
 
• The party is currently led by **N. Chandrababu Naidu**, who served multiple terms as the Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh.
 
• TDP has been a significant rival to YSRCP in the state’s political landscape.

questions.question: The three-age system for classification of pre-historic periods was introduced by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Christian Jurgensen Thomsen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Christian Jurgensen Thomsen was a Danish antiquarian and museum curator credited with introducing the **Three-Age System** of classification for prehistoric periods.
 
• The Three-Age System divides human prehistory into three major periods based on the primary material used for tools and weapons: **Stone Age, Bronze Age, and Iron Age**.
 
• Thomsen proposed this classification in the early 19th century while organizing collections at the **National Museum of Denmark**.
 
• The system was first published in 1836 in his book titled "**Ledetraad til Nordisk Oldkyndighed**" (Guide to Nordic Antiquity).
 
• His methodology involved detailed observation of artifacts, emphasizing the importance of **stratigraphy** and typology in archaeology.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Three-Age System:**

 
 
• The Stone Age refers to the earliest period, characterized by the use of stone tools.
 
• The Bronze Age marks advancements in metallurgy, with tools and weapons made primarily of bronze.
 
• The Iron Age represents the widespread use of iron for tools, weapons, and construction.
 
 
 
• **Stratigraphy:**
 
 
• Thomsen emphasized the importance of studying the layers of soil where artifacts were found.
 
• Stratigraphy helps archaeologists determine the relative age of objects based on their placement in different layers.
 
 
 
• **Typology:**
 
 
• Typology is the study of changes in artifact designs over time.
 
• Thomsen used typology to categorize tools and objects systematically.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Archaeology:**
 
 
• Thomsen’s Three-Age System laid the **foundation for modern archaeological methods.**
 
• It provided a chronological framework that is still used to study ancient civilizations.
 
 
 
• **Other Contributors:**
 
 
• While Thomsen introduced the system, later archaeologists like **Jens Jacob Asmussen Worsaae** confirmed its validity through fieldwork.
 
• Worsaae's work established the importance of excavations in validating the Three-Age System.

questions.question: What is a primary deficit?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Total deficit minus interest payments**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Primary deficit** is defined as the fiscal deficit of the government excluding the interest payments on previous borrowings.
 
• The formula for primary deficit is: **Primary Deficit = Fiscal Deficit - Interest Payments.**
 
• It is an indicator of the government's borrowing requirements for meeting expenses other than interest payments.
 
• A high primary deficit implies that the government is borrowing not only to pay interest on past loans but also to cover current expenses.
 
• This measurement is critical for assessing the sustainability of government debt and indicates if the borrowing trend is manageable in the long term.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Revenue deficit**

 
 
• Revenue deficit represents the shortfall in government revenue receipts compared to its revenue expenditure.
 
• The formula for revenue deficit is: **Revenue Deficit = Revenue Expenditure - Revenue Receipts.**
 
• This indicates that the government is unable to meet its operational expenses through its revenue income, which could lead to borrowing for routine expenditures.
 
 
 
• **Fiscal deficit**
 
 
• Fiscal deficit is the difference between the government's total expenditure and total revenue (excluding borrowings).
 
• The formula for fiscal deficit is: **Fiscal Deficit = Total Expenditure - Total Revenue (excluding borrowings).**
 
• It reflects the overall borrowing requirement of the government in a fiscal year.
 
• A high fiscal deficit can lead to inflation and increased debt burden for the economy.
 
 
 
• **Capital expenditure**
 
 
• Capital expenditure refers to the funds utilized by the government for acquiring fixed assets or investing in long-term infrastructure projects.
 
• Examples include investments in roads, schools, hospitals, and other developmental projects that contribute to economic growth.
 
• Capital expenditure is essential for boosting productivity and ensuring sustainable economic development.

questions.concept: Socio - Religious Reform Movements in the 19th and 20th CE India
questions.question: The Anushilan Samiti and Jugantar were associated with which type of activities?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Revolutionary activities**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Anushilan Samiti and Jugantar were prominent revolutionary organizations formed during the Indian independence movement, particularly in Bengal.
 
• Anushilan Samiti was established in 1902, while Jugantar emerged as its offshoot in 1906, advocating armed resistance against British colonial rule.
 
• These groups focused on activities such as bomb-making, armed revolts, and targeted assassinations of British officials, aiming to weaken the British administration.
 
• Prominent leaders like Aurobindo Ghosh, Barindra Ghosh, and Bagha Jatin played key roles in these revolutionary movements, inspiring nationalism and self-sacrifice among Indians.
 
• Despite British suppression, these groups created significant awareness and laid the foundation for future movements for India's independence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Brahmo Samaj (1828):**

 
 
• Founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy; worshipped one eternal God, opposed priesthood/rituals, promoted reason.
 
 
 
• **Arya Samaj (1875):**
 
 
• Founded by Swami Dayanand Saraswati; rejected idolatry, polytheism, rituals, emphasized Vedic teachings.
 
 
 
• **Satyashodhak Samaj (1873):**
 
 
• Founded by Jyotirao Phule; aimed to save Shudras/Ati-Shudras from Brahmanical exploitation, promoted education.
 
 
 
• **Ramakrishna Mission:**
 
 
• Led by Swami Vivekananda; emphasized spiritual knowledge, service, and human unity.

questions.question: The bacteria conducting an anoxygenic photosynthesis use which of the following compounds as an electron donor?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hydrogen sulphide**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Anoxygenic photosynthesis is a type of photosynthesis performed by certain bacteria where oxygen is not released as a by-product.
 
• Bacteria conducting anoxygenic photosynthesis use hydrogen sulphide (H2S) as an electron donor instead of water.
 
• During this process, hydrogen sulphide is oxidized to produce elemental sulfur (S) or sulfate (SO4²⁻) as a by-product.
 
• These bacteria possess specialized pigments like bacteriochlorophylls to absorb light energy and drive photosynthesis in anaerobic environments.
 
• Anoxygenic photosynthesis typically occurs in environments with low oxygen levels, such as deep-sea sediments, hot springs, or sulfur-rich regions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Glucose:**

 
 
• Glucose is an organic compound and a primary energy source for most living organisms.
 
• It is utilized during cellular respiration but is not used as an electron donor in photosynthesis.
 
• In oxygenic photosynthesis, glucose is synthesized as a product of the Calvin Cycle.
 
 
 
• **Carbon dioxide:**
 
 
• Carbon dioxide (CO₂) is a key reactant in photosynthesis, used in the Calvin Cycle to form glucose.
 
• It is not an electron donor but acts as a carbon source for both oxygenic and anoxygenic photosynthesis.
 
 
 
• **Water:**
 
 
• Water (H₂O) is used as an electron donor in oxygenic photosynthesis by plants, algae, and cyanobacteria.
 
• It undergoes photolysis, releasing oxygen (O₂) as a by-product.
 
• Anoxygenic photosynthesis, however, does not use water as an electron donor.
 
 
 
• **Anoxygenic Photosynthesis:**
 
 
• This process is carried out by bacteria like purple sulfur bacteria, green sulfur bacteria, and heliobacteria.
 
• Electron donors include hydrogen sulphide, ferrous iron, or organic compounds, depending on the environment and bacterial species.
 
• It plays a crucial role in sulfur and nutrient cycling in anaerobic ecosystems.

questions.question: In which year did the Government of India launch the National Youth Policy (NYP) to address the needs of India's youth?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2014**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Government of India launched the **National Youth Policy (NYP) in 2014** to cater to the needs and aspirations of the youth in India.
 
• The policy focuses on individuals aged **15 to 29 years**, who make up around 27.5% of the population, highlighting its significance in national development.
 
• **NYP 2014** prioritizes areas such as education, skill development, employment, entrepreneurship, health, and sports to empower the youth.
 
• The policy aims to ensure **inclusive development** by addressing the needs of marginalized and disadvantaged youth and involving them in nation-building activities.
 
• Implementation is done through collaboration between various ministries, state governments, and private organizations, leveraging schemes like Skill India and Start-Up India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Key Objectives of NYP 2014:**

 
 
• To develop a productive and skilled workforce that can contribute to economic growth.
 
• To promote social values and community engagement among the youth.
 
• To ensure equitable access to resources and opportunities for youth, irrespective of their socioeconomic background.
 
• To encourage youth participation in governance, decision-making processes, and leadership roles.
 
 
 
• **Priority Areas under NYP 2014:**
 
 
• **Education:** Focus on providing universal access to quality education and vocational training.
 
• **Skill Development:** Emphasis on improving employability through skill-building programs.
 
• **Employment & Entrepreneurship:** Creating opportunities for entrepreneurship and self-employment.
 
• **Health:** Addressing the physical, mental, and emotional well-being of the youth.
 
• **Sports:** Promoting competitive sports and physical fitness programs.
 
 
 
• **Implementation of NYP 2014:**
 
 
• The policy encourages collaboration with private organizations and industries.
 
• It integrates existing government initiatives like Start-Up India, Digital India, and Skill India for achieving its objectives.

questions.question: The maximum strength of the legislative council of the state is fixed at ______ of the total strength of the State Legislative assembly.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**one-third**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The maximum strength of the Legislative Council in a state is fixed at **one-third of the total strength of the State Legislative Assembly**, as per Article 171 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The Legislative Council is the **upper house of the State Legislature**, similar to the Rajya Sabha at the national level.
 
• The minimum strength of the Legislative Council cannot be less than **40 members**, regardless of the size of the Legislative Assembly.
 
• The Legislative Council is a **permanent body** and cannot be dissolved, but one-third of its members retire every two years.
 
• Currently, only six states in India have a Legislative Council: **Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Telangana, and Uttar Pradesh**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Composition of the Legislative Council:**

 
 
• One-third of the members are elected by the members of local bodies such as municipalities and district boards.
 
• One-third are elected by the members of the Legislative Assembly of the state.
 
• One-twelfth are elected by graduates of three years’ standing residing in the state.
 
• One-twelfth are elected by teachers of three years’ standing in the state who are not lower in standard than secondary school.
 
• The remaining members are nominated by the Governor from among persons having special knowledge or practical experience in fields like literature, science, art, cooperative movement, and social service.
 
 
 
• **Purpose of the Legislative Council:**
 
 
• The Legislative Council acts as a **revising chamber** for legislation passed by the Legislative Assembly.
 
• It provides a platform for experienced and qualified individuals, who may not contest direct elections, to contribute to the legislative process.
 
 
 
• **Abolition or Creation of Legislative Councils:**
 
 
• A state legislature can pass a resolution by a **special majority** (two-thirds of the members present and voting) to either create or abolish a Legislative Council.
 
• This resolution is sent to the Parliament, which can approve it by passing a law.
 
 
 
• **Legislative Council vs. Legislative Assembly:**
 
 
• The **Legislative Assembly** is the directly elected lower house, while the **Legislative Council** is the indirectly elected upper house of the State Legislature.
 
• Unlike the Legislative Assembly, the Legislative Council is a **permanent body** and is not subject to dissolution.

questions.question: Tura is situated on which hill, which comes under the mild extremely humid agroclimatic zone?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Garo Hills**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Tura is located in the **Garo Hills**, which is part of the state of Meghalaya in northeastern India.
 
• The Garo Hills come under the **mild extremely humid agroclimatic zone**, characterized by high rainfall and lush vegetation.
 
• It serves as the **largest town** and administrative headquarters of the West Garo Hills district.
 
• The region is rich in biodiversity, with dense forests and a wide variety of flora and fauna contributing to its humid climate.
 
• The Garo Hills are home to the **Garo tribal community**, known for their matrilineal society, cultural heritage, and traditional practices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Laur Hills:**

 
 
• The Laur Hills are not located in Meghalaya and are not associated with Tura.
 
• They are lesser-known and not recognized as a major geographical feature in the northeastern region of India.
 
 
 
• **Jaintia Hills:**
 
 
• Located in Meghalaya, the Jaintia Hills are known for their limestone deposits and caves.
 
• This region has a distinct cultural identity, with the Jaintia tribal community residing here.
 
• The Jaintia Hills are part of the Meghalaya Plateau and receive significant rainfall, but they are not categorized under the mild extremely humid agroclimatic zone.
 
 
 
• **Khasi Hills:**
 
 
• The Khasi Hills, also located in Meghalaya, are known for their unique matrilineal society and vibrant cultural festivals.
 
• Shillong, the capital of Meghalaya, is located in the Khasi Hills.
 
• Though the Khasi Hills share similar climatic conditions with the Garo Hills, they do not encompass Tura or the mild extremely humid agroclimatic zone.

questions.question: Internationally acclaimed Bharatanatyam dancer, Padma Subrahmanyam, was awarded with which of the following awards in 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Padma Vibhushan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Padma Subrahmanyam**, a globally recognized Bharatanatyam dancer, was conferred with the prestigious **Padma Vibhushan** in 2024 for her immense contributions to the field of Indian classical dance.
 
• The Padma Vibhushan is the **second-highest civilian award** in India, honoring "exceptional and distinguished service" in diverse fields, including arts, literature, and public affairs.
 
• Padma Subrahmanyam is renowned for her pioneering research on the **Natya Shastra**, blending traditional elements with innovative techniques in Bharatanatyam.
 
• She developed a unique style called **"Bharata Nrityam,"** which incorporates ancient dance movements depicted in sculptures and texts.
 
• Previously, she was honored with the **Padma Shri (1981)** and **Padma Bhushan (2003)**, recognizing her lifelong dedication to the Indian classical dance tradition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Padma Shri**

 
 
• The Padma Shri is the **fourth-highest civilian award** in India, instituted in 1954.
 
• It is awarded for distinguished contributions in various fields, including arts, education, sports, medicine, social work, and public affairs.
 
• Padma Subrahmanyam was awarded the Padma Shri in 1981 for her contributions to Bharatanatyam.
 
 
 
• **Padma Bhushan**
 
 
• The Padma Bhushan is the **third-highest civilian award** in India.
 
• It recognizes "distinguished service of a high order" in any field.
 
• Padma Subrahmanyam received the Padma Bhushan in 2003 for her exemplary work in Indian classical dance and scholarship.
 
 
 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award**
 
 
• This award is considered the highest recognition in the field of performing arts in India.
 
• It is presented by the **Sangeet Natak Akademi**, India's national academy for music, dance, and drama, to individuals who have made outstanding contributions to these fields.
 
• Padma Subrahmanyam has also been honored with this award in recognition of her contributions to Bharatanatyam.
 
 
 
• **Bharatanatyam**
 
 
• Bharatanatyam is one of the oldest classical dance forms in India, originating in Tamil Nadu.
 
• It draws heavily from the **Natya Shastra**, the ancient Indian treatise on performing arts written by Bharata Muni.
 
• Traditionally performed in temples, Bharatanatyam combines intricate footwork, graceful movements, and expressive gestures (abhinaya) to depict stories, often based on Hindu mythology.

questions.question: Raas-Leela symbolises which classical dance based on the spiritual and eternal love of Radha and Krishna?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Manipuri**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Manipuri** is one of the eight recognized classical dance forms of India, originating from the northeastern state of Manipur.
 
• The dance form is deeply rooted in the **Vaishnavite traditions** of the region, revolving around devotion and spirituality.
 
• The **Raas-Leela** in Manipuri portrays episodes from the life of Lord Krishna, focusing on the eternal and divine love between Radha and Krishna.
 
• It is characterized by soft, graceful, and fluid movements, emphasizing expressiveness and storytelling over dramatic gestures.
 
• Traditional Manipuri costumes, such as the Potloi (cylindrical skirts for women) and dhoti for men, add to the aesthetic appeal of the dance form.
 
• Musical accompaniment includes traditional instruments such as the Pung (drum), Kartal (cymbals), and harmonium, which enhance the devotional atmosphere.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kuchipudi**

 
 
• Kuchipudi is a classical dance form from Andhra Pradesh, India, blending dance, music, and acting.
 
• It is known for its narrative storytelling, often featuring mythological and spiritual themes.
 
• Performers use intricate footwork and graceful movements, accompanied by dialogues and songs.
 
• Kuchipudi performances often include dramatic enactments of Hindu epics like the Ramayana and Mahabharata.
 
 
 
• **Sattriya**
 
 
• Sattriya, originating from Assam, is a classical dance form introduced by the Vaishnavite saint Srimanta Sankardeva.
 
• It is performed in monasteries called Satras and emphasizes devotion to Lord Krishna.
 
• The dance includes rhythmic movements, storytelling, and traditional Assamese music.
 
• Sattriya costumes are simple yet elegant, reflecting the spiritual essence of the dance.
 
 
 
• **Chhau**
 
 
• Chhau is a semi-classical dance form from eastern India, including states like Odisha, Jharkhand, and West Bengal.
 
• The dance is known for its vigorous movements, martial art elements, and use of masks (in certain styles).
 
• It depicts episodes from epics like the Ramayana and Mahabharata, as well as folk tales and themes.
 
• Chhau dance is performed during festivals and rituals, showcasing the cultural richness of the region.
